question.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cosine function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcosh}⁡x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(12\operatorname{arcosh}⁡(\frac{x}{6})) \\  & =12\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcosh}⁡(\frac{x}{6})) \\  & =12\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{{(\frac{x}{6})}^{2}-1}}\cdot {(\frac{x}{6})}^{′} \\  & =12\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{\frac{{x}^{2}}{36}-1}}\cdot \frac{1}{6} \\  & =\frac{12}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}-36}}.\end{aligned}
$$
